questions.question: What type of object is the Sun?
choices: A rocky planet
A star
A natural satellite
A comet

questions.question: Which planet is largest in the solar system?
choices: Earth
Mars
Jupiter
Venus

questions.question: Which force keeps planets in their orbits around the Sun?
choices: Gravity
Magnetism alone
Friction
Air pressure

questions.question: Which group consists entirely of the four inner planets?
choices: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn
Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars
Mercury, Earth, Saturn, Neptune

questions.question: Where is the main asteroid belt?
choices: Inside the Sun
Between Earth and Venus
Beyond every known planet
Between Mars and Jupiter

questions.question: What does a planet's rotation mean?
choices: Its spinning about its axis
Its journey around the Sun
Its changing distance from the Sun
Its orbiting of the center of the galaxy

questions.question: What does a planet's revolution mean?
choices: The formation of its atmosphere
Its orbital motion around another object
Its daily spin
Its surface warming during a day

questions.question: Why do most planets shine in visible-light images?
choices: They reflect sunlight
They reflect only light from their moons
Their atmospheres create all incoming light
They produce sunlight by fusion in their cores

questions.question: How does a comet often develop a visible tail near the Sun?
choices: Its rocky surface produces a tail by nuclear fusion
Its icy material freezes more rapidly near the Sun
Solar heating releases gas and dust from its icy material

choices: It is the only object that rotates
It contains most of the system's mass and strongly influences orbits
It produces all gravity in the universe
Its visible light pushes planets into circular paths

questions.question: How do the inner planets differ from Jupiter and Saturn?
choices: The inner planets have no solid material
The inner planets are all larger
The inner planets orbit outside the gas giants
The inner planets are rocky, while Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants

questions.question: What mainly powers the Sun's energy output?
choices: Nuclear fusion in its core
Chemical reactions between rocks
Friction with orbiting planets
Combustion of oxygen at its surface

questions.question: Why does an orbiting planet not simply fall straight into the Sun?
choices: Its atmosphere blocks solar gravity
It lies beyond the reach of gravity
Its sideways motion combines with gravitational acceleration
It is held up by the solar wind alone

questions.question: What is a natural satellite?
choices: A small star outside the galaxy
An object such as a moon that orbits a larger body
A planet that has no atmosphere
Any object that reflects light

questions.question: What does one astronomical unit approximately represent?
choices: The diameter of the Sun
The distance from Earth to the Moon
The distance light travels in one year
The average Earth–Sun distance

questions.question: Two planets orbit the Sun; one is much farther away. What generally follows?
choices: The farther planet has a shorter year
The farther planet has a longer orbital period
The farther planet must rotate more slowly
Both must have identical orbital periods

questions.question: An object orbits Jupiter and does not produce energy by sustained stellar fusion. How is it most likely classified?
choices: A moon
A star
A constellation
An inner planet

questions.question: A student says that all planets have solid surfaces like Earth. Which observation challenges this claim?
choices: Mars has a rocky surface
Venus reflects sunlight
Mercury orbits the Sun
Jupiter's outer layers are predominantly gases

questions.question: Which comparison correctly separates an asteroid from a comet in typical composition?
choices: Asteroids contain mostly ice; comets contain only metal
Asteroids are mainly liquid; comets are mainly gas
Asteroids are mostly rocky or metallic; comets contain substantial ice as well as dust and rock
Asteroids are larger than planets; comets are their moons

questions.question: A planet completes one rotation much faster than Earth. What can be inferred about its rotation period?
choices: Its year must also be shorter
Its orbit must lie closer to the Sun
Its mass must be greater than Earth's
